Khac Phu Nguyen

WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Walmart, the retail giant (NASDAQ:WMT), ruled out using AI to charge shoppers different prices based on who they are or when they buy. Shares fell about 2.6% to $105.86 around 11:30 a.m. ET Tuesday. The message is blunt: Sparky may help customers shop, but it will not decide that one customer should pay more than another.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with WMT.

WMT GF Value chart

CEO John Furner's letter says income, purchase history and urgency will not push up an individual's price. Walmart also says its shopping tools will not bury cheaper options, while employees will oversee pricing and test the technology. As Barron's reported, the company is drawing a public boundary around AI pricing. That puts its promise of consistent low prices ahead of a tempting new use for customer data.

The valuation gap is small: at $105.86, the shares sit 1.58% above the $104.21 GF Value estimate. That leaves investors with a practical question. If Walmart keeps personalized pricing off the table, can better search, recommendations and inventory decisions generate enough value from AI to justify the spending?

title: Has Costco Stock Become the New Recession-Resilient Retail King?
detail:
Has Costco Stock Become the New Recession-Resilient Retail King?
Geoffrey Seiler, The Motley Fool
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 9:50 AM PDT 4 min read
COST
WMT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) has long been considered a place for investors to park money in the retail space when consumers are under stress, but after its stock fell more than 8% in the session following its fiscal Q1 results and more than 9% after its fiscal Q2 results, that baton may have been passed to a close rival: Costco Wholesale (NASDAQ: COST).

Costco posted another quarter of solid results and was up 7% year-to-date as of Sept. 25, while Walmart is down 3%. Below, I'll take a closer look at the retailer's fiscal Q4 results and prospects to see if this is the recession-resistant retailer to own.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Momentum continues

Costco continues to deliver strong results, with e-commerce sales leading the way. Adjusted digital revenue surged nearly 20%, with U.S. digital sales climbing more than 20%, helped by the company's partnerships with Uber Technologies and DoorDash.

Overall, the company's fiscal Q4 revenue jumped 11% to $95.7 billion, and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) rose 12% to $6.60, excluding a $0.15 benefit from tariff refunds. That was ahead of the analyst consensus for EPS of $6.55 on revenue of $95.7 billion.

Same-store sales jumped by 6.7% when adjusting for changes in gasoline prices and foreign currency. U.S. same-store sales climbed 7.2% (adjusted), while Canadian comparable-store sales rose 4.6% (adjusted). Other international same-store sales increased by 6.2% (adjusted).

Excluding gasoline and currency impacts, Costco's average transaction rose 3.3%, led by a 3.9% rise in the U.S. Traffic also increased by 3.3%, led by a 4.5% increase in international markets, while the U.S. saw a 3.2% gain. The retailer said that spending remained resilient in discretionary categories where it provides good value. It called out travel, jewelry, and major electronics as all seeing strong growth. Pharmacy sales also outperformed.

Membership-fee revenue jumped nearly 8% year over year, excluding currency movements, in the quarter to reach $1.85 billion. This was helped by a membership fee increase that it has now lapped. Meanwhile, paid memberships rose by nearly 4% to 84.1 million paid households. Higher-cost Executive membership climbed to 42.4 million members. These customers account for just over 50% of total paid memberships and made up 75.6% of Costco's worldwide sales.

title: Walmart Stock Trades 20% Below Its High: Here’s the Path to $128 by 2029
detail:
Walmart Stock Trades 20% Below Its High: Here’s the Path to $128 by 2029
Rexielyn Diaz
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 9:31 AM PDT 5 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Walmart Stock Trades 20% Below Its High: Here's the Path to $128 by 2029 ©Unai Huizi from Imágenes de unaihuizi and Leung Cho Pan via Canva
Key Stats for WMT Stock

Past week performance: -1.6%

52-week range: $99 to $135

Valuation model target price: $128

Implied upside: 17.5% over 2.3 years

Walmart's Earnings Beat Hasn't Won Back Investors Yet

Walmart (WMT) shares slipped about 1.6% over the past week, closing near $109 on Monday. The stock now sits roughly 20% below its 52-week high of $135. That gap opened in August, when shares fell 8.9% to $104 on the day Walmart reported Q2 results. Since then, the recovery has been slow and uneven.

The August selloff was not about weak sales. Revenue rose 5.9% to $187.9 billion, adjusted EPS jumped 19.1% to $0.81, and global eCommerce grew 23%. Yet investors questioned the quality of that beat, because tariff refunds flattered profits. These refunds are one-time repayments of import duties collected under emergency trade powers.

Management still sounds confident. On the earnings call, CEO John Furner said, "I'm even more bullish today as we see the pieces increasingly powering each other." He meant faster businesses like advertising, marketplace, and membership now reinforce the core stores. And Walmart raised its full-year outlook, guiding for adjusted EPS of $2.80 to $2.87.

Recent headlines added texture rather than direction. Walmart is upgrading Scintilla, its supplier data platform, into an AI tool that flags problems like empty shelves. Meanwhile, two senators asked the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to probe how its Sparky chatbot handles "Made in USA" claims. Going forward, the stock needs proof that profits can keep growing once tariff refunds fade.

Is WMT Stock Undervalued?
WMT Guided Valuation Model (TIKR)

Under valuation model assumptions realized through 1/31/29, the stock is modeled using:

Revenue Growth (CAGR): 5.2%

Operating Margins: 4.8%

Exit P/E Multiple: 33.7x

Based on these inputs, the model estimates a target price of $128, implying a 17.5% total return from the current share price of $109 and a 7.1% annualized return over the next 2.3 years.

A 7.1% annual return falls below the 10% bar, so Walmart looks fully valued at today's price. The problem is not the business but the entry multiple. Walmart trades at 36.3x next year's earnings, compared with a 10-year average P/E of 25.2x.

WMT Guided Valuation Model (TIKR)

The model assumes that premium shrinks to 33.7x by early 2029. That still sits well above the five-year average of 29.2x, because investors now reward Walmart's advertising and membership income. Those streams earn far higher margins than groceries, so they justify some premium.

Revenue growth of 5.2% a year is close to Walmart's five-year record of 4.9%. Meanwhile, the operating margin rises to 4.8% from 4.4% over the past year. That improvement depends on eCommerce becoming more profitable as delivery routes get denser.

Target Cuts Prices On Nearly 2,000 Products Ahead Of Holidays: A Look At The Key Highlights
Heera Hari

TGT
WMT
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Target is cutting prices across apparel, footwear and home products, with select items now priced at least 20% below last year's levels.

Target's Circle Deal Days will run Oct. 6 to Oct. 7 alongside Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days, while Walmart's Fall Deals event begins Oct. 5.

According to The Fly, Mizuho lowered Walmart's price target to $125 from $130 but maintained an 'Outperform' rating, citing the early-stage impact of agentic AI on shopping behavior.

Target Corp. (TGT) announced Tuesday that it is lowering prices on nearly 2,000 home, apparel, and accessories items as holiday shopping gets underway, adding to more than 10,000 price reductions the retailer has made over the past year.

Target (TGT) shares were down 1.19% at the time of writing on Tuesday, while Walmart Inc.(WMT) stock was down 2.45%.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

The latest reductions cover women's, men's, infant and toddler apparel, shoes and home products. Target said select apparel items are now priced 20% or more below last year's levels.

The company said pricing, promotions and availability may vary by location and Target.com, and that the program excludes Alaska and Hawaii.

Walmart, Target Ramp Up Holiday Promotions

Target's latest price cuts come as major retailers ramp up promotions ahead of the holiday shopping season. Walmart is scheduled to run its Fall Deals event from Oct. 5 to Oct. 11, while Target's Circle Deal Days will run Oct. 6 to Oct. 7, coinciding with Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days.

The retail push comes against a backdrop of weaker U.S. consumer confidence. The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September from 88.6 in August, marking its lowest reading since 2014. Consumers also became less positive about current business conditions and the labor market during the month.

Meanwhile, Mizuho analyst David Bellinger lowered Walmart's price target to $125 from $130 while maintaining an 'Outperform' rating.

According to TheFly, the analyst made the adjustment after attending RetailClub's AI conference. Bellinger said Mizuho expects agentic AI to increasingly influence shopping behavior, while noting that the impact is still in its early stages.

TGT, WMT: Retail View

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained 'Bearish' for WMT over the past 24 hours, with message volumes at 'Normal' levels. Meanwhile, TGT maintained a 'Bullish' sentiment rating, with 'Normal' message volumes.

Quick Read

AWS grew 37% to $42 billion, its fastest growth in 18 quarters, and Andy Jassy sees it becoming a trillion-dollar annual revenue business.

Amazon beats Walmart on growth rate and valuation, while AWS is accelerating faster than Azure despite Microsoft posting 43% cloud growth last quarter.

Free cash flow turned negative as capex surged 68% to $54 billion, but operating cash flow still rose 40% to offset the concern.

Read More: Avoid these 13 retirement mistakes before they derail your future (sponsor)

I have added to my Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) position after every recent earnings report, and I have no plans to stop. Some investors worry the stock got expensive reaching its old highs. To me, those highs were the price of an older company. The Amazon I own today rents, designs, and sells the computing power behind artificial intelligence, and it also runs a retail and advertising business.

Sean Gallup / Getty Images News via Getty Images
AWS Acceleration Keeps Pulling Me Back

Amazon Web Services is what keeps bringing me back. AWS revenue rose 37% to $42.23 billion in the second quarter, its fastest pace in 18 quarters. Growth over the last four quarters ran 20%, 24%, 28% and 37%. Backlog reached $496 billion, and management said most AWS capacity for 2027 is already reserved. Andy Jassy said during the call that AWS "very possibly" becomes "a trillion dollar annual revenue business for us in time."

Three Reasons the Data Backs Me Up

First, profits are growing faster than sales. Operating income rose 43% to $27.46 billion on revenue growth of 19.6%. AWS posted a 39.4% operating margin, so the fastest-growing unit also makes the most on each dollar of sales.

Second, advertising gives me a second engine. Ad revenue grew 26% to $19.81 billion, and growth has held between 23% and 26% for four straight quarters.

title: Costco's US Comp Sales Lead as Domestic Momentum Stays Strong
detail:
Costco's US Comp Sales Lead as Domestic Momentum Stays Strong
Sumit Singh
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 8:01 AM PDT 3 min read
COST
TGT
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Costco Wholesale Corporation COST continued to see strong momentum in its core U.S. market during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, with domestic comparable sales growth leading other operating regions. U.S. comparable sales increased 10.7% year over year, ahead of the company's overall comparable sales growth of 9.4%. Adjusted U.S. comparable sales, excluding the impact of gasoline prices and foreign exchange, rose 7.2%, highlighting continued strength in underlying member demand.

The U.S. performance reflected balanced gains in both shopping frequency and average transaction value. During the quarter, U.S. comparable traffic increased 3.2%, while the average ticket advanced 7.3%. On an adjusted basis, traffic growth remained unchanged at 3.2%, while adjusted ticket growth stood at 3.9%. These trends indicate that Costco's domestic sales growth was supported by both higher member visits and increased spending per transaction.

Management noted that member spending remained resilient, with adjusted comparable sales, excluding gas and foreign exchange, consistently running in the 6%-7% range. The company also highlighted that nonfood sales were the strongest-performing category during the quarter, reflecting member response to quality products and value offerings.

Costco's U.S. comparable sales strength came as the company maintained its focus on delivering value across merchandise categories. Price reductions implemented during the quarter, including select everyday items, were part of efforts to return value to members following tariff refunds. The combination of higher traffic, larger baskets and continued member engagement supported Costco's domestic sales momentum in the final quarter of fiscal 2026.

Walmart & Target's Comp Sales Show Traffic Momentum Strength

Walmart Inc. WMT continued to deliver steady U.S. comparable sales momentum, with Walmart U.S. comp sales rising 2.6% in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, supported by higher transactions and unit volumes. Walmart reported a 1.5% increase in transactions and a 1.1% rise in the average ticket, while e-commerce remained a key contributor. Walmart U.S. e-commerce sales advanced 24%, reflecting continued strength in digital fulfillment and marketplace growth.

Target Corporation TGT posted comparable sales growth of 3.8% in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, supported by a 3.6% increase in comparable traffic. Target's digital comparable sales rose 8.7%, led by more than 25% growth in same-day delivery, while comparable store sales increased 2.7%. Target also highlighted broad-based strength across merchandise categories as it continued investing in value, convenience and its retail experience.

Costco's Sales Momentum Builds as Q4 Traffic and Ticket Rise
Sumit Singh
Tue, September 29, 2026 at 7:22 AM PDT 3 min read
COST
TGT
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Costco Wholesale Corporation COST demonstrated strong sales momentum in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, driven by gains in shopping frequency and average transaction value. Net sales reached $93,873 million, up 11.2% year over year. Total company comparable sales expanded 9.4%. On an adjusted basis — excluding the impacts of gasoline price changes and foreign exchange fluctuations — comparable sales grew 6.7% across the company.

A primary catalyst for this top-line growth was balanced growth between global store traffic and ticket sizes. Worldwide traffic, or shopping frequency, increased 3.3% during the 16-week fourth quarter ended Aug. 30, 2026. The average transaction size, or ticket, rose 5.9% globally. When adjusted for gasoline prices and foreign exchange, the average ticket advanced 3.3% worldwide.

Regional segment performance highlighted broad-based strength in customer activity. In the United States, reported comparable sales climbed 10.7%, supported by a 7.3% increase in ticket and a 3.2% rise in traffic. On an adjusted basis, U.S. comparable sales were up 7.2%, with ticket rising 3.9% and traffic up 3.2%. Canada reported adjusted comparable sales growth of 4.6%, backed by a 2.1% ticket gain and a 2.5% traffic rise. Other International markets recorded an adjusted comparable sales increase of 6.2%, with traffic expanding 4.5% and ticket rising 1.7%.

Costco's performance was strong across warehouses, ancillary businesses and digital platforms. Digitally-enabled comparable sales saw significant gains, jumping 19.5% on a reported basis and 19.8% when adjusted for changes in foreign exchange rates.

Costco's fourth-quarter comparable sales growth was supported by a balanced contribution from higher member visits and increased spending per transaction.

Competitor Sales Momentum: Walmart & Target

Walmart Inc. WMT also saw sales growth supported by higher customer activity and digital momentum. Walmart U.S. comparable sales increased 2.6% in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, driven by higher transactions, while average ticket rose 1.1%. Globally, Walmart reported 23% growth in e-commerce sales, reflecting continued strength in pickup, delivery and marketplace channels.

Target Corporation TGT reported improving traffic trends in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, with comparable sales rising 3.8%, driven by a 3.6% increase in comparable traffic. Target also recorded an 8.7% improvement in comparable digital sales, supported by same-day delivery growth of more than 25%. Target noted that top-line strength was broad-based across channels and categories, with all six core merchandising categories growing year over year.
